site.title: Parla — clear voice in every web call
site.description: Parla is a free, open-source browser extension that uses AI to remove background noise from your microphone in any web calling app. The AI runs on your device; your audio never leaves it.
site.lead: Parla uses AI to remove background noise and other voices from your microphone in Meet, Teams, Zoom and any other web calling app. The AI runs right on your device: your audio never leaves it.
site.note: Free and open source · No account · No sign-up
site.how.title: How it works
site.how.sub: The extension sits between the calling app and your microphone. Every app gets the cleaned voice, without changing anything in the app.
site.how.ai.p: Neural networks trained to tell voices from noise run in your browser with WebAssembly. Nothing is uploaded, nothing is recorded.
site.how.any.p: Works wherever a site asks for your microphone. Turn it on or off per site from the toolbar.
site.how.quality.p: Full-band speech (48 kHz), background voices and noise removed, with a delay of a few hundredths of a second.
site.how.safe.p: If anything goes wrong, your call simply keeps the plain microphone. Updates wait until your call ends.

install.title: Install Parla
install.description: Install the Parla extension for Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari: free, open source, no account.
install.lead: Parla is free and open source. Add it from your browser's store: it installs in a click and updates itself.
install.chrome: Download the zip and unzip it. Open {ext} (in Edge: {edge}), turn on Developer mode, click Load unpacked and choose the unzipped folder.
install.firefox: Download the zip. Open {url}, click This Firefox, then Load Temporary Add-on… and choose the zip. Firefox removes it when it restarts.
install.store.chrome: Install it with one click from the Chrome Web Store. Edge, Brave and Opera install it from there too.
install.store.firefox: Install it with one click from Firefox Add-ons (Firefox 140 or newer).
install.manual: Or install the release file yourself
install.safari: Coming soon to the App Store.
install.after: Then pin Parla to the toolbar and start a call: it is on for every site. Click its icon to see how much noise it removes, change the quality or turn it off for a site.
site.install.sub: Free for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari: add it in a click from the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons.
site.open.title: Open source
site.open.sub: The engine, the extension and the models it runs are open: Apache-2.0 code, model weights under their own permissive licences. Read it, build it, improve it.
privacy.title: Parla — privacy
privacy.description: Parla processes your microphone on your device. The extension sends no reports unless you turn them on.
privacy.short: Short version: your voice is processed on your device and goes only to the call you are in. The extension sends nothing unless you turn on its anonymous technical reports (errors, performance); it never sends audio, page content or what you type.
privacy.ext.1: Audio from your microphone is processed inside your browser, on your computer. It is never uploaded, stored or recorded.
privacy.ext.2: The engine and its models ship inside the extension. Apart from the reports described below, it makes no network requests of its own.
privacy.ext.3: There is no account and no sign-in. We don't know who uses Parla.
privacy.ext.4: Your settings (on/off per site, quality, strength, language) are kept by your browser's extension storage, synced by your browser if you have that turned on.
privacy.ext.5: The extension asks to run on all websites so that it can wrap the microphone wherever a calling app asks for it. It reads no page content.
privacy.rep.1: Anonymous technical reports are off unless you turn them on in the extension's settings: errors, performance (delay, processing time), the settings you use, your browser and operating system, and the kind of calling app (for example "Meet" or "other") — never its address. They carry a random ID that changes every month.
privacy.rep.2: Detailed diagnostics are off unless you turn them on: they add the domain of the site where Parla ran (for example meet.google.com, never the rest of the address) and a permanent random ID, so a problem on one site can be traced.
privacy.rep.3: Reports go to a small receiver of ours on Cloudflare. It keeps the reports for at most 7 days and a summary without page addresses for at most 3 months. It does not store IP addresses. Audio, page content and anything you type are never sent.
privacy.site.1: No cookies, no analytics, no trackers.
privacy.site.2: The live demo processes your microphone in this page; the audio never leaves your browser.
privacy.site.3: The video on the home page loads from YouTube (privacy-enhanced mode) only when you click play.
privacy.open.p: You don't have to take our word for it: the complete source is public. Questions: open an issue on the project's repository.
demo.title: Parla — try it live
demo.description: Hear Parla clean your own microphone, live in your browser. Nothing leaves your device.
demo.lead: Talk with some noise around you: typing, a fan, music, other people. Parla's AI cleans your microphone right here in this page; nothing is sent anywhere.
demo.started: Microphone on: noise suppression is running.
demo.note: Runs on your device with WebAssembly. Works best in Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
demo.err.blocked: Microphone access was blocked. Allow it in the address bar and try again.
demo.err.unsupported: This browser can't run the engine (it needs WebAssembly and AudioWorklet). Try Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
